evidence: Defines mutable online hypothesis plus immutable commit to replace one-shot alarm-like emission.
Models start, ongoing, ending, completed, and commit as a lifecycle.
OAT shows early online proposals and boundary refinement; CESR must go beyond by logging revision and commit lifecycle.
ActionSwitch uses state changes for boundaries; CESR must distinguish by revisable hypothesis and commit ledger.
PCEH attempted endpoint/emission separation, but current implementation lacks valid risk-set targets.
Event-centric prefix episodes and feature cache are selected to control full-packet training cost.
Frozen feature cache removes repeated visual forward from Stage 1 training.
LoRA is the selected PEFT route for adapting pretrained vision model after frozen-stage evidence.
OZ-TAL already covers online zero-shot/open-vocabulary TAL using off-the-shelf VLM.
OnPoint already covers offline-to-online TAL distillation; use only as ablation/support.
Memory and history baselines are strong; selection must beat same-budget random/uniform/motion baselines.
Smoke reported packet/update/causal replay pass for frozen/adaptor route.
Cancelled/slow pilots support need for cheaper training protocol, not the final method claim.
No formal result exists yet; claim is unproven until experiments are run.
CAG-QIL establishes sequential decision history and MDP state as prior art; CESR must add identity belief trajectories and stopping utility.
SimOn establishes lightweight recurrent online state prediction and start/end grouping as prior art.
ProTAS establishes progress-aware causal prediction refinement in adjacent online segmentation.
OpenHOUSE blocks generic hierarchical streaming action-semantics novelty.
Thinking-QwenVL blocks generic causal state, hypothesis revision, and when-to-respond novelty.
StreamReady blocks generic readiness-aware streaming response timing novelty.
Online event-level memory and low-latency temporal grounding are adjacent prior art.
ETAD supports selective gradient/proposal sampling and warns against distribution-distorting label-guided sampling.
Separates physical endpoint from first causally sufficient evidence time.
Introduces explicit sequential false-commit or coverage risk at adaptive stopping times.
Uses anytime-valid risk control as a possible statistical foundation, subject to valid video-level assumptions.
Completion moment and incompletion motivate separating semantic completion evidence from physical action end.
First-sufficient-evidence timing is adjacent prior art in streaming VideoQA; the candidate must remain instance-localization and risk specific.
Readiness-aware timing is adjacent; direct risk-controlled temporal span localization remains the intended delta.
Allocates frame rate, resolution, or depth from expected localization-risk reduction.
SAN is the required adaptive-compute precedent and baseline.
Extends causal inference to chronological domain/class shifts with delayed sparse feedback.
OZ-TAL covers unseen classes without continual adaptation; the candidate must isolate adaptation and forgetting.
StreamFormer blocks generic causal streaming-backbone pretraining as a new headline.
SelectStream blocks generic budgeted streaming evidence memory as a headline claim.
Targets long-horizon false-alarm risk and detection delay in continuous semantic-video monitoring.
WACV 2026 already applies an e-process with provable false-alert control to a real-time video failure-detection task; semantic event structure must supply the nontrivial delta.
WATCH is a mandatory conformal-martingale baseline for risk-delay monitoring.
Sequential false-alarm control already exists in online video anomaly detection.
Separates physical transition, visual observability, and algorithmic commit times.
Force-synchronized egocentric video may provide privileged physical timestamps for a pilot.
Defines the earliest legal decision for a missing required event under deadlines or irreversible states.
Moves adaptive compute before pixel acquisition and constrains missed-event and delay risk.
Introduces delayed event-level feedback, future-only adaptation, and immutable historical outputs.
PaSBench already aligns first visible danger, accident boundaries, and causal warning timing; PIVOT needs an independent physical clock and population interval.
APT already defines and temporally localizes atomic physical transitions tied to visual evidence and mechanisms.
Ego4D PNR already provides PRE, CONTACT, PNR, POST, and state-change keyframe localization.
TouchMoment makes precise contact-only event spotting insufficient as a new task.
Synchronized head and wrist views plus pressure maps could identify view-conditioned physical-to-visual gaps if data become available.
Initial, transition, and end state localization are established; PIVOT must contribute measurement decomposition.
STARE already establishes latency-aware evaluation and ranking reversals in streaming perception.
Train-time multimodal supervision with RGB-only inference is established and cannot be claimed as novelty.
Probabilistic temporal boundaries are established; PIVOT needs a population observability object rather than generic uncertainty.
Multi-rater temporal boundary diagnostics motivate interval and population-level annotation.
Video-time and wall-clock output latency must be separated because streaming latency accounting is established.
Jointly trains a strict causal raw-video encoder and identity-preserving action-instance tracker under standard On-TAD output rules.
Prefix-parallel causal chunks replace packet-wise optimizer events while incremental inference retains cache state.
Multiple persistent event slots explicitly represent overlapping and repeated same-class action instances.
MATR is the direct instance-level query/window baseline; PETAL must replace fresh-window rediscovery with persistent query trajectories.
ActionSwitch already addresses overlapping same-class actions; PETAL must win with identity-linked trajectories under matched features.
E2E-LOAD proves raw-video end-to-end streaming OAD is feasible but does not localize action instances.
StreamFormer occupies generic causal streaming-backbone training; PETAL's delta must be instance-level trajectory learning and joint On-TAD adaptation.
Static birth queries, persistent identity queries, and set assignment are existing tracking mechanisms; Stage 1 must beat a matched temporal reconstruction.
The full route is demoted until a frozen-feature FRESH/TTF/PES falsification study isolates the value of On-TAD-specific persistence.
The preregistered G0 compares dynamic-birth replay with full video-start gold, fixed context, and reset under matched code, data, checkpoint, suffix, and stochasticity.
Three of four samples violated absolute loss, gradient, and runtime-state fidelity, so the current dynamic-birth CRS-EPS surrogate cannot remain primary training under its frozen contract.
The sampled surrogate diverged from full chronological gold before profiling, triggering C4's explicit failure criterion for the current protocol.
CSFSB abandons empty-state replay and preserves complete chronological state while retaining event sampling only for loss and backward contributions.
CSFSB tests whether full causal forward with selective backward can reduce training cost without changing the chronological state trajectory.
The clean 160x3 audit found 2,206 actual GT-birth exhaustions; independent review rejected the sole zero-exhaustion arm as degenerate birth suppression and selected KILL_Q2_R1.
The omitted-history failure motivates preserving every chronological state transition and sampling only gradient contributions.
R-A uses one model-only prefix state in train and inference while keeping GT assignment ephemeral and loss-only.
Continuous occupancy, first completion, release-before-reseed, and immutable commit model the full On-TAD event lifecycle.
Multiple latent carriers and same-class overlap/repetition gates test instance separation without GT runtime identity.
Anti-silence readiness jointly constrains recall, precision, counts, duplicate, fragmentation, and all-background false emissions.
Before any model P0, route evidence must establish data prevalence, cached-feature causality, B0-B4 fairness, structural OOD, negative controls, and non-equivalence to temporal MOTR.
Q2's runtime/canonical lifecycle mismatch and silent capacity escape motivate loss-only assignment over a model-only state.
CRS-EPS omitted-history failure requires complete chronological forward state rather than empty-state replay.
Temporal TrackFormer/MOTR reconstruction is the strongest novelty attack; R-A must show an On-TAD-specific immutable lifecycle benefit beyond persistent queries.
MOTR already propagates track queries and assigns existing/newborn instances; R-A must show a matched temporal reconstruction cannot reproduce its observable lifecycle gains.
TadTR already establishes direct action-query interval prediction, so action queries and interval heads are baseline ingredients rather than R-A novelty.
